title: CKY TV film of object jumping from the ground to 5,000 ft
summary: Grant Cameron tells of CKY TV film of object jumping from the ground to 5,000 ft, about May 1975 at Carman, Manitoba, Canada, and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: So in May the CKY film was caught on film. They caught this thing jumping from the ground to 5,000 ft in the air in three frames, four frames.
May 13th, 1975. Cameraman Alan Carr of station CKY in Manitoba photographs two separate sightings over Carman in front of four witnesses.
tellings.difference: Gives the date as 13 May 1975, names the cameraman as Alan Carr and says four witnesses saw two separate sightings.
tellings.link_reason: Same CKY filming of the Carman object in May 1975 as telling 7, here narrated in the documentary.

as_told.title: CKY film editor's account of filming the object

plain: In May 1975, near the small town of Carman in Manitoba, Canada, someone from CKY, a local TV station, filmed something odd in the sky. A Canadian UFO researcher, Grant Cameron, says the film shows an object leaping from the ground to 5,000 feet in the air in just three or four frames. A well-known researcher, Jacques Vallee, is also quoted from a work called UFOs: It Has Begun. He gives the date as 13 May 1975 and says a cameraman named Alan Carr filmed two separate sightings over Carman, with four witnesses present. Cameron adds that when he spoke to the man who shot the film, he learned he was not a cameraman at all but a film editor at the studio. If the footage shows what they say, something moved far faster than any known aircraft.
